title: Everything I Carry Every Day (2026 Edition)
creator: Marcus Bell
description:
Pocket dump time. Phone, keys, wallet, sling, and the one thing that got stolen this year.

Thanks to Ekster for sponsoring this video! Get 20% off with code MARCUS20: https://ekster.com/marcus

Full gear list in the pinned comment.

sentences.t: What's up everybody, Marcus here, and today I'm emptying my pockets for you, because last year's everyday carry video is officially out of date.
A lot changed, some stuff got lost, one thing got stolen, and a couple of things I just stopped using.
So let's go pocket by pocket.
Front left pocket is always my phone, and this year that's the same phone as last year, because I'm trying to keep it for four years.
I put it in a slim case with a ring on the back, mostly because I drop it about once a day.
Front right pocket is keys, and I finally got these under control.
I used to have this giant jangly ring with a bottle opener and a tiny flashlight and three loyalty cards.
Now it's a little key organizer that folds everything into one stack, and it's quiet, which my coworkers appreciate.
Back pocket is my wallet, and this is a good time to mention that today's video is sponsored by Exter.
This is the Exter Parliament wallet, and the trick is this little trigger on the side.
Click it and your cards fan out, so you can grab the one you need without digging around.
It's aluminum and leather, it holds up to twelve cards, and it blocks RFID, so nobody's skimming your cards on the subway.
The new version also has a slot for a tracker card, so if you lose it, it shows up on your phone's map.
After my last wallet got lifted on a train in Lisbon, that feature alone sold me.
Use code MARCUS20 at Exter dot com slash marcus for twenty percent off, and the link's in the description.
Okay, moving on to the bag, because I carry a small sling most days.
Inside the sling, there's a little pouch with the boring essentials, painkillers, plasters, lip balm, and a spare hair tie, which is for my girlfriend, not me.
Then there's my knife, which is a small slip joint with a short blade, so it's legal pretty much everywhere I go.
I mostly use it to open boxes, cut tags off clothes, and once to free a bird that got tangled in fishing line, which is the most heroic thing it's ever done.
Next, a pen, because I'm the person in every meeting who never has a pen, and I'm trying to change.
This one is a bolt action pen in brass, and it's slowly getting that nice worn patina.
Then earbuds, a flat charging cable, and a tiny power bank that's about the size of a lipstick.
The last thing is new this year, a little pocket notebook.
I've started writing things down instead of putting them in my phone, and I remember them so much better.
And that's it, that's everything I carry.
If I had to pick the one item that changed my day the most this year, it's honestly the key organizer, because I don't sound like a janitor walking down the hallway anymore.
Let me know what you carry, I read every comment on these.
And I'll see you in the next one.
